note: The one pack here that deliberately replaces bundled records rather than adding new ones. Every record sets "overrides": true and reuses a bundled name on purpose, so the pack is the corpus's test of declared replacement. Two consequences worth knowing. First, loaded with the bundled slice excluded there is nothing to replace, and the loader emits seven 'declares an override but nothing of that name is loaded' warnings — correct behaviour, not a defect in this file. Second, 'paralyzed' is carried here with the printed flags precisely so that our Hold Person still resolves under exclude; without it the spell would reference a condition no loaded pack defines, which is an error rather than a warning.

conditions.name: paralyzed
conditions.description: Carried unchanged from the printed condition. It is here so that this pack's Hold Person still has a condition to apply when the bundled slice is excluded.
unmodelled: Deliberately identical in effect to the bundled row; the record exists for load-order reasons, not to change the rules
A pack that applies a bundled condition should carry it if the pack is meant to load standalone

unmodelled: The printed condition also prevents moving closer to the source of fear
Replacing a bundled condition name is legal and changes it for every pack that applies it
